businessModel: KDE e.V. donations and volunteer work
updateCadence: KDE Gear: major releases in April, August, December plus monthly bugfix releases
summary: Falkon is the KDE project’s Qt WebEngine browser (the former QupZilla). It offers built-in ad blocking, a password manager integration and Python/QML plugins, but ships few headline features and has no extension store or sync.
bestFor: People wanting a simple Chromium-engine browser without Google services
Light use on Linux or Windows
notFor: Anyone who needs fast Chromium patching

pros.title: Built-in ad blocking
pros.detail: ABP-style filter lists included without extensions.

pros.title: KDE integration
pros.detail: Uses KDE wallets, themes and dialogs; follows Plasma look.

pros.title: Light and simple
pros.detail: Clean interface, speed dial, full-page screenshots.

cons.title: No WebExtensions
cons.detail: Plugins are Falkon-specific (Python/QML/C++), so the ecosystem is tiny.

cons.title: No sync
cons.detail: No built-in cross-device sync of bookmarks or tabs.

cons.title: Slow patch pipeline
cons.detail: Chromium fixes arrive via Qt WebEngine releases and distro packaging.

cons.title: Low development velocity
cons.detail: KDE Gear 26.08 changelogs show only maintenance changes for Falkon.

faq.a: Yes, through Qt WebEngine; Falkon itself is a Qt/C++ application.

Yes, KDE publishes Windows builds (Microsoft Store/CI), though Linux is the main platform.

timeline.event: Renamed Falkon and moved into KDE

switching.note: Imports bookmarks from Firefox, Chromium, Opera and others via the bookmark importer.

spec.drm: Widevine possible if Qt WebEngine build supports it
spec.patchLag: Follows Qt WebEngine and distro updates

pageLoad: Blink engine with a light UI
startup: Qt app start plus WebEngine init
lowEnd: Lighter UI than Chrome but same engine
patchSpeed: Lags via Qt WebEngine release cycle
tabManagement: Tab list and pinning; no groups
extras: Speed dial and a few plugins
